policies/copyright-dispute-policy.text: {{COMPANY}}は、{{PRODUCT}}上で著作権その他の権利の侵害が生じているとのお申出を受け付けています。この記事では、お申出に記載していただく事項、受付後の流れ、措置を受けた方が異議を申し出る手続をまとめます。 この手続の位置づけ {{PRODUCT}}の会議ノートは、原則としてアクセス権限のあるメンバーだけが閲覧できるもので、不特定の方に向けて公開されるものではありません。そのため本手続は、情報流通プラットフォーム対処法（平成13年法律第137号。旧「プロバイダ責任制限法」）の考え方を参考にしつつ、{{COMPANY}}の 利用規約 に基づく契約上の措置として実施しています。米国法に基づく削除手続ではありません。日本には、米国のような指定代理人の登録制度に相当する仕組みはなく、窓口の設置は{{COMPANY}}の自主的な運用です。 利用規約 禁止事項と利用停止の根拠 → ノートを共有する 共有範囲の設定と共有リンクの扱い → プライバシーポリシー 利用者情報の取扱い → 脆弱性開示ポリシー セキュリティに関する報告（本手続の対象外） → # 適用される法律の整理 情報流通プラットフォーム対処法は、「特定電気通信」による情報の流通によって権利侵害が生じた場合の枠組みを定めています。 法令 情報流通プラットフォーム対処法 第2条（定義） 「特定電気通信」は、不特定の者によって受信されることを目的とする電気通信の送信（公衆によって直接受信されることを目的とする電気通信の送信を除く）と定義されています。アクセス権限のある特定のメンバーだけが閲覧できるワークスペース内の会議ノートは、原則としてこの「特定電気通信」に当たりません。この部分については同法の枠組みが直接適用されないため、{{COMPANY}}は利用規約に基づく契約上の措置として対応します。 一方、不特定の方が閲覧できる形で共有リンクを発行している場合、その部分は「特定電気通信」に該当しうるものとして取り扱います。 法令 情報流通プラットフォーム対処法 第3条（損害賠償責任の制限） 権利を侵害する情報の送信を防止する措置を講じた場合における発信者に対する損害賠償責任について、同条第2項は、権利が侵害されたとする者から侵害情報等を示して措置を講じるよう申出があったことを発信者に照会し、照会を受けた日から7日を経過しても発信者から措置に同意しない旨の申出がないときは、責任を負わないものとする旨を定めています。{{COMPANY}}がこの記事の「受付後の流れ」で照会手続に7日間の期間を設けているのは、この考え方を参考にしたものです。 法令 著作権法 第21条（複製権）／第23条（公衆送信権等） 著作者は、著作物を複製する権利および公衆送信（自動公衆送信の場合における送信可能化を含む）を行う権利を専有します。お申出にあたっては、どの権利が侵害されているとお考えかをご記載ください。 削除基準の公表義務について 情報流通プラットフォーム対処法は、申出の受付方法の公表、調査、申出者への通知、送信防止措置の基準の公表といった義務を、総務大臣の指定を受けた「大規模特定電気通信役務提供者」に課しています。{{PRODUCT}}はこの指定の対象ではありません。本記事の内容は、法令上の義務として公表しているものではなく、{{COMPANY}}の自主的な運用として定めたものです。 # お申出に記載していただく事項 法定の様式はありません。次の各項目をご記載ください。項目が不足している場合、事実関係を確認できないため、補正をお願いすることがあります。 申出者の情報 — 氏名または名称、住所、連絡先（電話番号およびメールアドレス） 権利者との関係 — 申出者が権利者ご本人である場合はその旨。代理人としてお申出になる場合は、権利者の氏名または名称、および代理権限を証する書面 侵害されたとする権利の内容 — 著作権（複製権、公衆送信権など）、著作者人格権、商標権などの別 対象となる著作物の特定 — 題号、著作者名、公表の年月日、掲載場所など、当該著作物を特定できる情報 {{PRODUCT}}上の対象情報の特定 — 共有リンクのURL、ノートの識別子、該当箇所の記載など、対象を一意に特定できる情報 権利が侵害されたとする理由 — 申出者が権利者であること、対象情報が申出者の著作物の複製等であること、権利者が利用を許諾していないこと 真実性の表明 — 記載内容が真実であり、虚偽の申出により{{COMPANY}}または発信者に損害が生じた場合には申出者が責任を負うことを認める旨 申出年月日および署名 — 記名押印、または電磁的方法によるこれに準ずる措置 # 申出書の記載例 そのまま書き写してご利用いただけます。 侵害情報の通知書兼送信防止措置依頼書 {{COMPANY}} 御中 申出年月日: 〔申出書を作成した年月日〕 1. 申出者 氏名または名称: 住所: 電話番号: メールアドレス: 権利者本人／代理人（代理人の場合は権利者名と代理権限を証する書面を添付）: 2. 侵害されたとする権利 （例）著作権（複製権・公衆送信権） 3. 対象となる著作物 題号: 著作者名: 公表年月日: 公表の場所（URL・書誌情報など）: 4. 対象情報の所在 共有リンクのURL／ノートの識別子: 該当箇所: 5. 権利が侵害されたとする理由 6. 表明 上記の記載内容は真実です。虚偽の申出により{{COMPANY}}または発信者に 損害が生じた場合には、申出者が責任を負うことを認めます。 署名または記名押印: 虚偽の申出について 事実に反するお申出により、掲載した利用者または{{COMPANY}}に損害が生じた場合、申出者が損害賠償の責任を負うことがあります。権利の帰属と侵害の有無を十分にご確認のうえ、お申出ください。 # 送付先 項目 内容 宛先 {{COMPANY}} 法務担当 郵送先 {{ADDRESS}} メール {{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}（件名に「著作権侵害の申出」とご記載ください） 権利侵害のお申出はこの窓口で受け付けます。脆弱性に関するご報告は受付の経路と対応の手順が異なり、{{SECURITY_EMAIL}}宛にお送りいただきます。範囲と手続は 脆弱性開示ポリシー をご覧ください。 # 受付後の流れ 1 受付 お申出はメールまたは書面で受け付けます。受け付けた日時をお申出者にお知らせします。 2 形式の確認 記載事項に不足がある場合、補正をお願いすることがあります。補正がなされるまでの間、以降の手続は進行しません。 3 発信者への照会 対象情報を掲載した利用者（発信者）に対し、お申出の内容をお示しして、送信を防止する措置を講じることに同意されるかどうかを照会します。照会を受けた日から7日を経過しても、発信者から同意しない旨のお申出がない場合、{{COMPANY}}は送信を防止する措置を講じることがあります。 4 判断と措置 権利侵害が明らかであると判断した場合、または前の段階の照会手続を経た場合、{{COMPANY}}は、対象情報の公開の停止、共有リンクの無効化その他の措置を講じます。 5 結果の通知 措置の内容とその理由を、お申出者と発信者の双方にお知らせします。 6 異議の申出 措置を受けた利用者は、{{COMPANY}}に対して異議を申し出ることができます。手続はこの記事の「措置を受けた場合の異議の申出（再開の手続）」に定めています。 7 繰り返しの侵害への対応 権利侵害を繰り返すアカウントについては、利用規約第12条および第19条に基づき、本サービスの利用停止または契約の解除を行うことがあります。 発信者への照会を省略する場合 権利侵害が明らかである場合、または発信者に照会することによって被害の拡大その他の不利益が生じるおそれがある場合には、照会を経ずに措置を講じることがあります。この場合も、措置を講じた後に発信者へ通知します。 # 措置を受けた場合の異議の申出（再開の手続） 対象情報を掲載した利用者は、措置の内容に異議がある場合、次の事項を記載して{{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}宛にお申し出ください。 申出者（発信者）の氏名または名称、住所、連絡先 措置の対象となった情報の特定（措置前の共有リンクのURL、ノートの識別子など） 措置が誤りであるとお考えの理由（自ら著作権を有する、権利者から許諾を得ている、引用として適法である、対象情報が申出者の著作物ではない、など） 記載内容が真実であることの表明 申出年月日および署名または記名押印 {{COMPANY}}は、異議の内容を確認し、権利侵害がないと判断した場合には、措置を解除して対象情報を元の状態に戻します。判断が困難な場合は、お申出者と発信者の双方に、当事者間での協議または司法手続による解決をご案内します。 米国の手続との違い 米国法に基づく手続では、反論の通知を受けてから一定の営業日数の経過をもって自動的に復旧するという仕組みが採用されています。日本にはこれに対応する法定の期間がないため、{{COMPANY}}は、期間の経過によって自動的に復旧させるのではなく、内容を確認したうえで判断します。 # 引用として適法な場合 {{PRODUCT}}に保存された資料や会議の発言に第三者の著作物が含まれている場合でも、その利用が引用として適法であれば、権利侵害には当たりません。 法令 著作権法 第32条第1項（引用） 公表された著作物は、引用して利用することができます。この場合の引用は、公正な慣行に合致し、かつ報道、批評、研究その他の引用の目的上正当な範囲内で行われるものでなければならないと定められています。 「社内利用だから私的複製」という整理はできません 著作権法第30条の私的使用のための複製は、個人的または家庭内その他これに準ずる限られた範囲での使用を対象としています。企業や団体における業務上の利用はこれに当たりません。社外から入手した資料を{{PRODUCT}}にアップロードする際は、社内での利用が許諾の範囲内かどうかをご確認ください。 # 発信者情報の開示請求について {{COMPANY}}は、利用者の情報を、法令に基づく場合を除いて第三者に開示しません。発信者情報の開示をお求めの場合は、情報流通プラットフォーム対処法第5条に基づく開示請求、または同法第8条に基づく発信者情報開示命令の申立てをご検討ください。裁判所の発信者情報開示命令その他の法令に基づく手続があった場合、{{COMPANY}}は法令に従って対応します。この場合、法令上可能な範囲で、対象となる利用者にその旨をお知らせします。 法令 情報流通プラットフォーム対処法 第5条（発信者情報の開示請求）／第8条（発信者情報開示命令） 権利を侵害されたとする者は、一定の要件のもとで、開示関係役務提供者に対して発信者情報の開示を請求することができ、また裁判所に対して発信者情報開示命令の申立てをすることができます。{{COMPANY}}が任意に開示に応じることはありません。 # 権利者がとりうる法的手段 法令 著作権法 第112条・第114条・第119条第1項（差止請求・損害額の推定・罰則） 著作権者は、侵害の停止または予防を請求することができます。損害賠償を請求する場合の損害額については推定の規定が置かれています。また、著作権を侵害した者に対する罰則として、10年以下の拘禁刑もしくは1000万円以下の罰金、またはこれらの併科が定められています。 {{COMPANY}}による措置は、契約上の対応にとどまります。権利の帰属や侵害の有無について当事者間に争いがある場合の最終的な判断は、裁判所によります。 # うまくいかないときは 対象を特定できないと言われた — 共有リンクのURL、またはノートの識別子をご記載ください。画面の説明だけでは対象を一意に特定できないことがあります。 対象のノートが閲覧できない — 非公開のワークスペース内のノートは、{{COMPANY}}の側でも、権限のない者が内容を閲覧することはできません。お申出の内容にもとづいて調査を行います。 回答がない — 補正をお願いしている場合、補正がなされるまで手続が進行しません。お送りいただいた内容と{{COMPANY}}からの連絡の有無をご確認のうえ、{{SUPPORT_EMAIL}}宛に再度ご連絡ください。 # 関連記事 利用規約 — 禁止事項、利用停止および契約の解除 ノートを共有する — 共有範囲と共有リンクの設定 プライバシーポリシー — 利用者情報の取扱いと開示の考え方 脆弱性開示ポリシー — セキュリティに関する報告の窓口と手続

policies/data-processing-addendum.description: The addendum setting out {{COMPANY}}'s obligations as a processor, sub-processing, cross-border transfers and security measures.
policies/data-processing-addendum.html:
Where a corporate customer uses {{PRODUCT}}, {{COMPANY}} stands as the party entrusted with processing the personal data that the customer handles as a personal information handling business operator. This addendum sets out, in the form of contract provisions, both parties' rights and obligations in relation to that entrustment. It covers everything a customer needs in order to supervise its processor under Article 25 of the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (“the Act”).

Note

This addendum is a template. Before it is executed, {{COMPANY}}'s legal team must review its contents and settle the items left blank. The [ ] in the text are fields to be completed on execution: the controller's corporate name (recital), the record retention period (Article 8), the notice period and objection period for sub-processors (Article 9), the deadline for assisting with requests (Article 11), the breach notification deadline (Article 12), the audit conditions (Article 13), the deletion deadline (Article 15), the liability cap (Article 16) and the list of sub-processors (Schedule 3).

This addendum forms part of the terms of service. Where this addendum and the terms of service differ on a matter concerning the processing of personal data, this addendum prevails. The terms of service apply to everything else. Personal information that {{COMPANY}} handles as a personal information handling business operator in its own right is governed by the privacy policy.

[the customer's corporate name] (“the controller”) and {{COMPANY}} (“the processor”) conclude this data processing addendum (“this addendum”) as follows, in relation to the controller entrusting the processing of personal data to the processor in connection with the controller's use of {{PRODUCT}} (“the service”).

#Chapter 1 General provisions

#Article 1 (Purpose and scope)

  1. The purpose of this addendum is to set out the rights and obligations of the controller and the processor so as to ensure that personal data the controller has the processor handle in connection with use of the service is processed in compliance with the Act and other relevant legislation.

  2. The parties confirm that the controller's provision of personal data to the processor, and the processor's handling of it, constitute provision in connection with entrustment under Article 27, paragraph 5, item 1 of the Act, and are not provision to a third party under paragraph 1 of that article.

  3. This addendum forms part of the terms of service and the other contracts between the controller and the processor concerning provision of the service (“the contract”).

  4. Where this addendum and the contract conflict on a matter concerning the processing of personal data, this addendum prevails. The contract applies to everything else.

  5. This addendum applies to personal data the controller handles in the service as a personal information handling business operator. It does not apply to personal information the processor obtains for its own business and handles for purposes it determines itself (the names and contact details of the controller's staff, billing and invoicing information, information about service availability and the like), which is governed by the processor's privacy policy.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 27, paragraph 5, item 1 (restriction on provision to third parties)

Where personal data is provided in connection with entrusting all or part of its processing within the scope necessary to achieve the purpose of use, the recipient is not a “third party”. Consent is therefore not required for provision on the basis of entrustment. The controller, on the other hand, comes under a duty to supervise the processor under Article 25 of the Act, and the processor may not process personal data beyond the scope of the work entrusted.

#Article 2 (Definitions)

In this addendum, the following words have the meanings given below. Words not defined here have the meanings given in the Act and in the contract.

  1. Personal information means personal information as defined in Article 2, paragraph 1 of the Act: information about a living individual that can identify a specific individual by name or other description (including anything expressed by voice, movement or other means), including information that can readily be collated with other information and thereby identify a specific individual.

  2. Personal data means personal data as defined in Article 16, paragraph 3 of the Act — that is, personal information constituting a personal information database.

  3. Sensitive personal information means sensitive personal information as defined in Article 2, paragraph 3 of the Act: personal information including descriptions of the individual's race, creed, social status, medical history, criminal record, the fact of having suffered harm from a crime, or the other matters set out in Article 2 of the Enforcement Order.

  4. Personal information handling business operator means a personal information handling business operator as defined in the Act.

  5. Entrustment means entrusting all or part of the processing of personal data within the scope necessary to achieve the purpose of use, as referred to in Article 27, paragraph 5, item 1 of the Act.

  6. Controller personal data means personal data the controller has the processor handle in connection with use of the service. Its specific categories, the categories of individuals, the purposes of processing and the duration of processing are set out in Schedule 1.

  7. Sub-processor means a party to which the processor entrusts all or part of the processing of controller personal data, including any party to which a sub-processor in turn entrusts it (and so on down the chain).

  8. Breach means leakage, loss or damage of controller personal data, including a situation where there is a risk that such a thing has occurred.

  9. Security measures means the necessary and appropriate measures taken under Article 23 of the Act to prevent breaches and otherwise keep personal data secure.

  10. Individual means a specific individual identified by controller personal data.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 2, paragraph 1 (definitions) / Article 16, paragraph 3 (definitions)

Personal information includes anything by which a specific individual can be identified from matters expressed by voice or other means. The general guidelines give recorded voice information that identifies a specific individual — because the person's name is included, for instance — as an example of personal information. The meeting audio, transcripts, notes and speaker names handled in the service can readily be collated with participants' names and calendar invitations, so they are normally personal information; and since they are stored in a form searchable per workspace, they are personal data too.

#Article 3 (What is entrusted)

  1. The controller entrusts the processing of controller personal data to the processor to the extent needed for the controller to receive the service, and the processor accepts that entrustment.

  2. The work entrusted, the categories of personal data processed, the categories of individuals, the purposes of processing and the duration of processing are as set out in Schedule 1.

  3. In providing controller personal data to the processor, the controller warrants that it was obtained properly in accordance with the Act and other legislation, and that the processor's handling of it is within the scope necessary to achieve the purpose of use the controller has specified.

  4. The controller is responsible for specifying, notifying or publishing the purpose of use and taking any other necessary steps, so that controller personal data is not processed beyond the purpose of use specified in advance.

  5. The controller is responsible for telling participants that meetings are being recorded and transcribed, and for obtaining individuals' consent where sensitive personal information may be recorded.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 17, paragraph 1 (specifying the purpose of use) / Article 20, paragraph 1 (proper acquisition) / Article 20, paragraph 2 (proper acquisition)

The purpose of use must be specified as far as possible when handling personal information, and acquisition by deception or other improper means is prohibited. Sensitive personal information must not be acquired without the individual's prior consent, save in limited exceptions such as where the law requires it. The party that gives notice to participants and obtains consent when recording meetings is the controller, which determines the purpose of use of the personal data itself.

Article 3, paragraphs 3 to 5 place responsibility for the lawfulness of acquisition and for dealings with individuals on the controller. How to think about telling participants, with sample wording, is set out in How far you can go with AI minutes (a guide for teams).

#Chapter 2 The processor's obligations

#Article 4 (Processing on the controller's instructions, and no use for other purposes)

  1. The processor is to process controller personal data only within the scope set out in the contract, this addendum and Schedule 1, and in accordance with the controller's instructions, and must not process it beyond that.

  2. The processor must not use controller personal data for any purpose other than performing the work entrusted. It is not to carry out processing beyond the scope of the entrustment, including analysis for its own business, producing statistics, or developing or improving AI models. Use for training AI models is dealt with in Article 14.

  3. The contract and this addendum constitute the controller's general instructions to the processor concerning the processing of personal data. Individual instructions going beyond the contract and this addendum are to be in writing (including electromagnetic record; the same below), and the parties are to agree separately on who bears the cost of carrying them out.

  4. Where the processor considers that an instruction from the controller would breach the Act or other legislation, it is to notify the controller without delay. In that case the processor may refuse to follow the instruction.

  5. Where the processor is required by law to process controller personal data, it is to notify the controller in advance, unless the law prohibits it from doing so.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 18, paragraph 1 (restriction by purpose of use)

A personal information handling business operator must not handle personal information beyond the scope necessary to achieve the specified purpose of use without the individual's prior consent. The general guidelines state that a party receiving personal data in connection with entrustment may not handle it for anything other than the work entrusted. Article 4, paragraphs 1 and 2 give effect to that restriction as a contractual obligation. For the controller's supervision, see the legislation quoted under Article 9.

#Article 5 (Restriction on disclosure to third parties, and responding to legal demands)

  1. The processor must not provide or disclose controller personal data to a third party without the controller's prior written consent, save for provision to sub-processors under Article 9 and as provided in the following paragraph.

  2. The processor may disclose controller personal data, to the extent necessary, only where required by law or where it receives a lawful and valid demand from a court, an investigating authority or another competent public body.

  3. Where the processor receives a demand under the preceding paragraph, it is to notify the controller before disclosing, so that the controller has the opportunity to object or take other steps, save where the law prohibits it or the matter is urgent.

  4. So far as possible, the processor is to ask the party making such a demand to approach the controller directly.

  5. The processor must not sell controller personal data under any guise.

#Article 6 (Security measures)

  1. The processor is to take the necessary and appropriate measures under Article 23 of the Act to prevent breaches of controller personal data and otherwise keep it secure.

  2. The measures in the preceding paragraph are as set out in Schedule 2, under the headings of organisational, personnel, physical and technical security measures and understanding the external environment, on the basis that a basic policy on the handling of personal data has been established and rules for its handling put in place.

  3. The processor may change the security measures in line with technological developments, changes in the threat landscape and industry standards, provided the level of the measures after the change is not materially below the level before it.

  4. Where the processor processes controller personal data in a foreign country, it is to understand that country's personal data protection regime and take the necessary and appropriate measures to keep the data secure. At the controller's request, the processor is to provide the controller with the name of that country, the name of the country the servers are in, and the measures taken in light of that understanding.

  5. In using the service, the controller is responsible for taking appropriate measures in relation to managing account and API credentials, setting permissions within its own organisation, and administrators' sharing settings.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 23 (security control measures) / Article 32, paragraph 1, item 4 (publication of matters concerning retained personal data)

A personal information handling business operator must take the necessary and appropriate measures to prevent the leakage, loss or damage of personal data and otherwise keep it secure. The annex to the general guidelines organises those measures into seven headings: establishing a basic policy, putting handling rules in place, and organisational, personnel, physical and technical security measures, plus understanding the external environment. Understanding the external environment requires that, where personal data is handled in a foreign country, the personal data protection regime of that country be understood and the necessary and appropriate measures taken. Where the controller publishes the measures it has taken under Article 32, paragraph 1, item 4 of the Act and Article 10, item 1 of the Enforcement Order, the information provided under Article 6, paragraph 4 is the basis for doing so.

#Article 7 (Supervision of staff and confidentiality)

  1. The processor is to exercise the necessary and appropriate supervision under Article 24 of the Act over staff who handle controller personal data.

  2. The processor is to limit the staff who handle controller personal data to those who need to for their work, and to impose confidentiality obligations on them by agreement. Those obligations survive the end of their employment.

  3. The processor is to provide training on the handling of personal data to staff who handle controller personal data, both when they start work and periodically.

  4. The processor must not use the controller's confidential information and controller personal data that come to its knowledge under this addendum for any purpose other than that of this addendum, and must not disclose or leak them to third parties. This obligation survives the end of this addendum.

  5. As regards information subject to the secrecy of communications that comes to the processor's knowledge in connection with those features of the service that carry exchanges between users, the processor and its staff will not obtain, use or disclose it, save where required by law or where there is other proper reason. This obligation continues both during and after employment.

LegislationTelecommunications Business Act, Article 4 (protection of secrecy) / Article 179 (penalties)

The secrecy of communications handled by a telecommunications carrier must not be violated, and a person engaged in the telecommunications business has a duty to keep secret what they learn of others during their employment, which continues after they leave. Breaches are subject to penalties. Those features of the service that carry exchanges between users, such as sharing notes and notifications, are treated as being within that article.

Which features of the service fall within the Telecommunications Business Act depends on how they are built. {{COMPANY}}'s current position, and whether registration is required, are set out in Our security arrangements.

#Article 8 (Creating and keeping records)

  1. So that how controller personal data is processed can be established, the processor is to create and keep records of the following.
  • Access to controller personal data (who accessed it, when, and what they did)
  • The granting, changing and removal of permissions
  • The copying, transfer and deletion of controller personal data
  • The provision of controller personal data to sub-processors

  1. The records in the preceding paragraph are kept for [ ] years. Where different kinds of record are kept for different periods, the period for each kind is set and notified to the controller on request.

  2. At the controller's request, the processor is to provide the controller with a summary of the parts of those records relating to controller personal data, to a reasonable extent. This does not apply to parts whose provision would risk prejudicing the processor's own security.

  3. Because the processing of controller personal data is entrustment under Article 27, paragraph 5, item 1 of the Act, no record of provision to a third party is created under Article 29. How a request for disclosure of records of provision to third parties is handled is set out in Article 11.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 29 (creating records of provision to third parties)

Where a personal information handling business operator provides personal data to a third party, it must as a rule create and keep a record of the provision. However, no record need be created for provision falling within the items of Article 27, paragraph 5 — that is, provision in connection with entrustment, business succession or joint use. Provision from controller to processor under this addendum falls within that, so no record of provision to a third party is created.

#Chapter 3 Sub-processing and provision to third parties in foreign countries

#Article 9 (Sub-processing)

  1. The processor may sub-process all or part of the handling of controller personal data to a third party. The form of consent for sub-processing is to be one of the following, and the parties agree on execution which applies.
  • Option A (individual consent) Before sub-processing, the processor is to notify the controller in writing of the sub-processor's name, the country it is in, the work to be sub-processed and the security measures the sub-processor will take, and to obtain the controller's written consent.
  • Option B (general consent with prior notice) By executing this addendum, the controller consents in advance to sub-processing to the sub-processors listed in Schedule 3. Where the processor intends to add or change a sub-processor, it is to update Schedule 3 and notify the controller at least [ ] days before the change.

  1. Where Option B applies, the controller may, within [ ] days of receiving notice, object in writing to the addition or change, giving reasonable grounds relating to the protection of personal data. Where no objection is made within that period, the controller is deemed to have consented.

  2. Where the controller objects under the preceding paragraph, the processor is to consider the grounds and use commercially reasonable efforts to address the controller's concerns. Where the processor cannot offer an alternative sub-processor and the controller's concerns are not resolved, the controller may terminate the contract as regards the affected part of the service without paying any penalty.

  3. The controller acknowledges that some sub-processors are essential to providing the service, and that objecting to the use of such a sub-processor may make all or part of the service unavailable.

  4. The processor is to conclude a written contract with each sub-processor imposing on it obligations at least equivalent to the processor's obligations under this addendum. That contract is to include at least the following.

  • A prohibition on processing beyond the scope of the work entrusted
  • The security measures to be taken
  • Supervision of staff and confidentiality
  • Notification to the processor where a breach occurs
  • The conditions for any further sub-processing
  • Return or deletion on termination

  1. The processor is to keep itself informed periodically of how sub-processors handle controller personal data, and to require corrective action where necessary.

  2. The processor is liable to the controller for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors as though they were its own.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 25 (supervision of processors)

Where a personal information handling business operator entrusts all or part of the handling of personal data, it must exercise the necessary and appropriate supervision over the party entrusted so that the personal data entrusted is kept secure. The general guidelines identify three elements of that supervision — selecting an appropriate processor, concluding a contract with it, and keeping informed of how it handles the personal data — and state that where the processor sub-processes, the controller is expected to keep itself informed of the identity of the sub-processor, the work sub-processed and how it handles personal data, by receiving reports from the processor or otherwise, and to supervise appropriately. Article 9, paragraphs 1 and 6 are there to make that possible.

About choosing a consent model

Option A (individual consent) gives the controller more control, but requires a consent process every time a sub-processor changes, which delays provision of the service. Option B (general consent with prior notice and a right to object) is the usual arrangement for cloud services, but depends on keeping the list in Schedule 3 permanently up to date. Decide which {{COMPANY}} will adopt, delete the other from the provisions, and decide where the Schedule 3 list is published (in this help centre, or on a dedicated page).

#Article 10 (Provision to third parties in foreign countries)

  1. The parties confirm that Article 28, paragraph 1 of the Act applies to provision in connection with entrusting the processing of personal data, and that entrustment does not take a provision outside that article.

  2. The processor may provide controller personal data to a sub-processor in a foreign country only where one of the following applies.

  • Provision to a country with an equivalent regime The country is one designated by rules of the Personal Information Protection Commission as having a personal data protection regime recognised as being of a standard equivalent to Japan's.
  • An adequate framework in place The sub-processor has in place a framework meeting the standards set by rules of the Personal Information Protection Commission.
  • The individual's consent The controller has obtained the individual's prior consent to provision to a third party in a foreign country.

  1. To ensure a framework meeting the standards in the preceding paragraph, the processor is to conclude a contract with each sub-processor in a foreign country ensuring the implementation of measures in line with the intent of Chapter 4, Section 2 of the Act.

  2. So that the controller can meet its own obligations under Article 28 of the Act and explain matters to individuals, the processor is to provide the controller, on request and without delay, with information on the following.

  • The name of the sub-processor in the foreign country
  • The name of the foreign country it is in
  • Whether that country has a personal data protection regime, and an outline of it (including whether it has any regime capable of significantly affecting individuals' rights and interests)
  • The categories of controller personal data provided to that sub-processor, and how often
  • An outline of the measures the sub-processor takes in line with the intent of Chapter 4, Section 2 of the Act (“equivalent measures”)
  • The means by which the processor ensures the implementation of those equivalent measures
  • How often and by what means the processor verifies this
  • Where any impediment to the implementation of the equivalent measures arises, that fact and an outline of it

  1. The processor is to verify, at least once a year, how sub-processors in foreign countries are implementing the equivalent measures and whether those countries have a personal data protection regime and what it contains.

  2. Where that verification shows an impediment to the implementation of the equivalent measures, the processor is to take the necessary and appropriate measures and, where it becomes difficult to ensure their continued implementation, to stop providing controller personal data to that sub-processor. In that case the processor is to notify the controller without delay.

  3. Where an individual asks the controller for information under Article 28, paragraph 3 of the Act, the processor is to provide the necessary information on the matters in paragraph 4 without delay, so that the controller can respond.

  4. Where the controller chooses the route of the individual's consent under paragraph 2, the processor is to provide the controller with the matters it must give the individual when obtaining consent (the name of the destination country, information on that country's personal data protection regime, and information on the measures the sub-processor takes).

  5. Where the processor adds or changes a sub-processor in a foreign country, it is to notify the controller of the matters in paragraph 4 in addition to following the procedure in Article 9.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 28, paragraphs 1 to 3 (restriction on provision to third parties in foreign countries)

Providing personal data to a third party in a foreign country requires the individual's prior consent as a rule. Without consent, either the country must be one designated by rules of the Personal Information Protection Commission as having a personal data protection regime of a standard equivalent to Japan's, or the third party must have in place a framework meeting the standards set by those rules. What paragraph 1 of that article excludes are the cases listed in the items of Article 27, paragraph 1; the items of paragraph 5 of that article, covering entrustment, business succession and joint use, are not excluded. Article 28 therefore applies even to entrustment, where the counterparty is a third party in a foreign country. Paragraph 3 requires that, where the adequate-framework route is used, the necessary measures be taken to ensure continued implementation of the equivalent measures, and that information about those measures be provided at an individual's request.

LegislationEnforcement Rules of the Act on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 16 (adequate framework) / Article 17, paragraph 2 (information provided when obtaining consent) / Article 18, paragraphs 1 and 3 (ensuring continued implementation of equivalent measures)

Rule 16 provides that an adequate framework means that implementation of measures in line with the intent of Chapter 4, Section 2 of the Act is ensured by appropriate and reasonable means, or that certification under an international framework has been obtained. Rule 17, paragraph 2 lists three matters to be provided when obtaining an individual's consent: the name of the destination country, information on that country's regime, and information on the measures the third party takes. Rule 18, paragraph 1 requires periodic verification of the implementation of the equivalent measures and of that country's regime, the taking of necessary measures where there is an impediment, and the cessation of provision where continued implementation becomes difficult to ensure. Paragraph 3 of that rule lists seven matters to be provided at an individual's request. Article 10, paragraphs 4 to 7 provide for the information the controller needs in order to meet those obligations.

The countries currently designated by rules of the Personal Information Protection Commission as having a personal data protection regime of a standard equivalent to Japan's are the European Union (excluding the United Kingdom) and the United Kingdom. Where controller personal data is provided to a sub-processor in any other country, either the adequate-framework route or the individual's consent under Article 10, paragraph 2 is required. Designations can change, so check what the Personal Information Protection Commission has published before executing this addendum.

Which suppliers in which countries controller personal data is actually provided to is set out in Schedule 3. The explanation for controllers is in the security and privacy FAQ, and the explanation for individuals is under “Provision to third parties in foreign countries” in the privacy policy.

#Chapter 4 Responding to individuals and to security breaches

#Article 11 (Responding to requests from individuals)

  1. The controller is responsible for responding to requests from individuals under Articles 33 to 35 of the Act (requests for disclosure of retained personal data, for disclosure of records of provision to third parties, for correction, addition or deletion of content, and for cessation of use, erasure or cessation of provision to third parties; “access requests”), and to complaints about the handling of personal information (Article 40).

  2. The processor is to assist the controller to a reasonable extent, on request, with extracting, copying, correcting, deleting and other work needed for the controller to respond to an access request. The processor is to endeavour to complete that assistance within [ ] business days of the controller's request.

  3. Where the processor receives an access request or a complaint directly from an individual concerning controller personal data, it is not to respond itself but is to direct that individual to the controller and, unless the law prohibits it, to notify the controller without delay. This does not apply where the controller has instructed otherwise in writing or where the law requires the processor to respond.

  4. Because the processing of controller personal data is entrustment and not provision to a third party, no record of provision to a third party is created under Article 29 of the Act. Where an individual requests disclosure of records of provision to third parties, the controller is to notify the individual without delay that no such record exists.

  5. The processor provides a feature in the service for outputting notes, transcripts and other data containing controller personal data in electromagnetic form. The controller may use that feature to respond to a request for disclosure.

  6. Where the assistance in paragraph 2 would involve excessive work for the processor, the parties are to discuss separately who bears the cost of it.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 33, paragraph 1 (disclosure) / Article 33, paragraph 5 (disclosure) / Article 34 (correction etc.) / Article 35, paragraph 5 (cessation of use etc.) / Article 38, paragraph 1 (fees) / Article 40 (handling complaints)

An individual may request disclosure of retained personal data by provision in electromagnetic form or another method prescribed by rules of the Personal Information Protection Commission, and may also request disclosure of records of provision to third parties. Article 34 provides for requests to correct, add to or delete content; Article 35, paragraph 5 provides for requests for cessation of use and the like where the personal data is no longer needed, where a breach has occurred, or where there is otherwise a risk of harm to the individual's rights or legitimate interests. Fees may be charged only for notification of the purpose of use and for requests for disclosure, not for requests for correction or for cessation of use. Article 40 requires a personal information handling business operator to endeavour to handle complaints about the handling of personal information appropriately and promptly, and to put arrangements in place for doing so.

About response times

Fill in the number of business days in Article 11, paragraph 2 to match {{COMPANY}}'s support arrangements. The law does not state a deadline by which a controller must reply to an individual's request, but the controller has to respond “without delay”, so in practice the processor's deadline for assisting is set shorter than that. Where you state indicative response times in Section 10 of the privacy policy, make the figures consistent with them.

#Article 12 (Responding to a breach)

  1. Where the processor learns that a breach of controller personal data has occurred or may have occurred, it is to notify the controller promptly, and in any event within [ ] hours of learning of it.

  2. That notification is to include the following, so far as known at the time. Where anything is not yet known, the processor is to report further promptly once it is.

  • An outline of the breach or suspected breach
  • The categories of controller personal data affected or potentially affected
  • The number of individuals whose controller personal data is affected or potentially affected
  • The cause
  • Whether there is secondary harm or a risk of it, and what it is
  • What has been done for the individuals concerned
  • What has been published
  • Measures to prevent recurrence
  • Any other relevant matters

  1. The processor is to take the measures needed promptly to prevent the breach spreading, investigate the cause and restore the position, and is to report progress and the outcome to the controller.

  2. Reporting to the Personal Information Protection Commission (both the preliminary and the final report) and notifying individuals in respect of controller personal data are for the controller to do. The processor's notification under paragraph 1 is made as a notification to the controller under the proviso to Article 26, paragraph 1 of the Act.

  3. Notwithstanding the preceding paragraph, where the parties agree in writing, the processor may report to the Personal Information Protection Commission and notify individuals on the controller's behalf. In that case the processor is to obtain the controller's approval of the contents in advance.

  4. The processor is to provide, without delay and on request, the information the controller needs in order to report to the Personal Information Protection Commission and notify individuals.

  5. Where either party intends to make a breach public, it is to discuss the timing, content and manner of publication with the other party in advance, save where publication is required by law or the matter is urgent.

  6. Notification, reporting and assistance under this article do not amount to an admission of responsibility by the processor for the incident.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 26, paragraph 1, proviso (reporting breaches etc.) / Enforcement Rules Article 7 (situations with a high risk of harm to individuals' rights and interests), Article 8 (reporting to the Personal Information Protection Commission), Article 10 (notifying individuals)

Where a breach of personal data occurs with a high risk of harm to individuals' rights and interests, a report to the Personal Information Protection Commission and notification of the individuals are required. Four categories must be reported: where sensitive personal information is involved; where there is a risk of financial harm; where the act was, or may have been, carried out with improper intent; and where more than 1,000 individuals are involved — each including situations where the thing may have occurred. Reporting has two stages: a preliminary report promptly after learning of the incident, and a final report within 30 days of learning of it (60 days where the act may have been carried out with improper intent). Where a party entrusted with processing personal data notifies the controller that such a situation has arisen, its own reporting obligation falls away. The general guidelines indicate that “promptly” for the preliminary report means roughly within three to five days.

About setting the notification deadline

Fill in the number of hours in Article 12, paragraph 1 to match {{COMPANY}}'s incident response arrangements. For the controller to make its preliminary report to the Personal Information Protection Commission “promptly” (roughly within three to five days, per the guidelines), the processor's notification has to come well before that. 24, 48 and 72 hours are all commonly used. Bear in mind too that transcripts can contain sensitive personal information, so even a single-record breach can be reportable.

About the audit conditions

Settle the blanks in Article 13, paragraphs 4 and 5 to conditions {{COMPANY}} can accept. Thirty days' notice and once a year are common. Choose whether the cost falls on the controller, or on the processor only where the processor is at fault.

Keep in paragraph 2 only those assessment reports and certifications that appear in the table of certifications and third-party assessments in Our security arrangements, and delete any not held. The same check is needed for Schedule 2, which should state only measures actually in place.

#Article 14 (No training of AI models or other processing beyond what is entrusted)

  1. The processor must not use controller personal data for the development, training, retraining or evaluation of AI models provided by the processor or by a third party.

  2. Such processing goes beyond the scope of the work entrusted. For the processor to carry it out, the controller would have to specify a purpose of use and obtain individuals' consent, or the data would have to be processed into pseudonymously or anonymously processed information under the Act; neither is within the scope of this addendum.

  3. Where the processor uses an inference service provided by an external supplier for transcription, summarisation or other generation, it is to provide in its contract with that supplier that data sent will not be used for any purpose other than generating the response, including the supplier's own machine learning.

  4. At the controller's request, the processor is to explain whether such a contractual provision exists and outline it.

  5. The controller is responsible for judging whether the summaries and other output the service generates are suitable for its intended use, and is to carry out the checks it needs before relying on that output.

Article 14, paragraphs 1 and 2 spell out what follows from the framework of entrustment quoted in Article 1, paragraph 2 and Article 4. Using meeting data received from a controller to train the processor's own AI models cannot be done within that framework. In addition, the alert on the use of generative AI services published by the Personal Information Protection Commission on 2 June 2023 asks businesses using generative AI to confirm that the use is within the scope necessary to achieve the specified purpose of use, and that the provider of the generative AI will not use personal data entered for machine learning; Article 14, paragraphs 3 and 4 correspond to that.

This article assumes a business plan (Team or Enterprise). On the free and personal plans, use for training is on by default and users can turn it off in settings themselves. How each plan is treated, and the steps for the setting, are set out in AI models and training data.

Controller personal data contained in backups is deleted progressively as the backup retention period expires, and deletion is complete no later than [ ] days after the date this addendum ends.

  4. At the controller's request, the processor is to give the controller a written statement that deletion has been completed.

  5. Notwithstanding the preceding paragraphs, information the law requires to be kept is retained for the period the law prescribes. In that case the processor is to notify the controller of the scope of the information retained, the legislation requiring it and the retention period, and to continue applying the security measures in this addendum to that information.

  6. While using the service, the controller may also delete controller personal data using the service's features, or set a retention period for transcripts. The default retention setting is no automatic deletion, and applying a setting across a whole workspace is available on the Enterprise plan. How to configure it is set out in Automatic transcript deletion.

  7. Where the controller requests return under paragraph 1 in a format or by a means other than the output features the service provides as standard, the parties are to discuss separately who bears the cost.

LegislationAct on the Protection of Personal Information, Article 22 (keeping data accurate etc.)

A personal information handling business operator must endeavour to erase personal data without delay once it is no longer needed. Deleting data on termination is what enables the controller to meet both that duty to endeavour and requests from individuals for cessation of use quoted under Article 11.

About the deletion deadlines

Fill in the numbers of days in Article 15, paragraphs 1 to 3 to match {{COMPANY}}'s deletion processing and backup design. Deletion from production and deletion from backups complete at different times, so they have to be stated separately. Do not state a number of days without checking how backup generations are managed.

#Chapter 6 General provisions

#Article 16 (Damages and limitation of liability)

  1. Where the controller or the processor causes loss to the other by breaching this addendum, it is liable to compensate that loss.

  2. The damages the processor owes the controller are capped at the total service charges paid by the controller to the processor in the [ ] months preceding the event giving rise to the loss. That cap does not apply where the processor has acted intentionally or with gross negligence.

  3. Where an individual or other third party makes a claim against the controller concerning controller personal data and the cause of that claim is the processor's breach of this addendum, the processor is to compensate the controller's loss within the limits of the preceding paragraph.

  4. The controller is responsible for the lawfulness, accuracy and quality of the acquisition of controller personal data, and for the lawfulness of the instructions it gives the processor. Where loss is caused to the processor as a result, the controller is to compensate it.

  5. Each party's liability under this addendum is limited to what arises from its own acts or omissions.

  6. This article prevails over the limitation of liability provisions in the contract.

About the cap, and the Consumer Contract Act

Settle the period in Article 16, paragraph 2 (12 months is common), and whether the cap is the total charges or a fixed amount, according to {{COMPANY}}'s policy. This addendum is a contract with corporate customers, so the Consumer Contract Act does not apply; but where it is applied uniformly in the form of standard terms, Article 548-2, paragraph 2 of the Civil Code may mean that a provision found to unilaterally harm the other party's interests is deemed not to have been agreed. Avoid setting the cap at a strikingly low level.

#Article 17 (Term and surviving provisions)

  1. This addendum takes effect on the day the controller begins using the service under the contract, and remains in effect until the later of the day the contract ends and the day the processor ceases processing controller personal data.

  2. After this addendum ends, Article 5 (restriction on disclosure to third parties, and responding to legal demands), Article 7, paragraphs 4 and 5 (confidentiality), Article 8 (creating and keeping records), Article 15 (measures on termination), Article 16 (damages and limitation of liability), Article 18 (governing law and jurisdiction) and this article continue in effect.

  3. This addendum may be varied by written agreement of both parties. Variations necessary to reflect amendments to legislation or changes to guidance from the Personal Information Protection Commission may, however, be made by the processor notifying the controller of the changed contents and the effective date before that date arrives. Where the controller does not agree to such a variation, it may terminate the contract before the effective date.

LegislationCivil Code, Article 548-4, paragraphs 1 and 2 (change of standard terms of contract) / Article 548-2, paragraph 2 (agreement to standard terms of contract)

A party who prepared standard terms may change the contents of the contract without individual agreement where the change is in the general interest of the other party, or where it does not conflict with the purpose of the contract and is reasonable in light of the need for it, the appropriateness of the changed content and other circumstances. In that case it must set an effective date and make known, by use of the internet or other appropriate means, that the terms are being changed, what they will say and when they take effect; a change has no effect unless that is done before the effective date arrives. In addition, a provision restricting the other party's rights or increasing their obligations, which is found to unilaterally harm their interests contrary to good faith, is deemed not to have been agreed. These provisions apply to contracts between businesses too.

#Article 18 (Governing law and jurisdiction)

  1. The formation and effect of this addendum are governed by Japanese law.

  2. The district court with jurisdiction over {{COMPANY}}'s head office ({{ADDRESS}}) is the exclusive court of agreed jurisdiction of first instance for disputes arising between the controller and the processor concerning this addendum.

LegislationCode of Civil Procedure, Article 11, paragraph 1 (agreements on jurisdiction) / Act on General Rules for Application of Laws, Article 7 (choice of governing law by the parties)

The parties may fix the court with jurisdiction by agreement, for the first instance only. The formation and effect of a juridical act are governed by the law of the place chosen by the parties at the time. As this addendum is a contract with corporate customers, it provides for exclusive agreed jurisdiction. Jurisdiction in relation to consumers is dealt with in the terms of service.

#Article 19 (Notices and discussion)

  1. Notices under this addendum are given by delivering a document, by email or by display within the service. A notice from the processor to the controller may be given to the contact details the controller has registered in the service.

  2. Notices from the controller to the processor are to be addressed to {{PRIVACY_EMAIL}}.

  3. Matters not provided for in this addendum, and any doubt as to its interpretation, are to be resolved by discussion between the parties in good faith.

  4. Even where part of this addendum is held void or unenforceable, the effect of the remaining provisions is unaffected. In that case the parties are to discuss how to achieve, in valid terms, what is closest to the intent of the void or unenforceable provision.

#Schedule 1 What is entrusted

This schedule sets out the categories of controller personal data, the categories of individuals, the purposes of processing and the duration of processing referred to in Article 2, item 6 and Article 3, paragraph 2.

#The work entrusted

In order to provide the service, the processor carries out the following processing of controller personal data.

  • Acquisition (capturing meeting audio, receiving file uploads, synchronising calendar information)
  • Storage, organisation and structuring
  • Transcription, summarisation and other generation
  • Search and display
  • Correction, addition and deletion on the controller's instructions
  • Encryption and other processing for security
  • Output and transmission to external services on the controller's instructions
  • Deletion

#Categories of personal data processed

Category What it covers
Meeting audio Audio data captured during a meeting. Processed only for as long as needed to produce the transcript, and deleted once that is complete
Transcripts Text generated from the audio, the times of utterances, and speaker labels
Notes Notes written by users, AI-formatted notes, summaries and action items
Participant information Participants' names, email addresses, organisations and display names
Calendar information Meeting titles, dates and times, locations, lists of invitees and attendees, and the description field
Uploaded files Material users bring into the service, and what it contains
Chat records What users enter into the service's chat feature, and the responses generated
Account information Users' names, email addresses, the workspaces they belong to, and permission settings
Usage logs Sign-in records, operation records, IP addresses, operating system and browser type, and desktop app version
About adjusting the table of categories

The above assumes the standard configuration of the service. Add to or remove from it to match what {{COMPANY}} actually collects. Where features generated from audio for speaker identification are retained, that category and its retention period must be added. Whether such features constitute an individual identification code depends on the implementation, so check with the legal team before adding them.

#Categories of individuals

  • The controller's officers and employees who use the service
  • The controller's officers and employees who took part in a meeting recorded using the service
  • The controller's clients, customers and other third parties who took part in a meeting recorded using the service, or who were mentioned during a meeting
  • People named in files the controller has uploaded and in calendar information it has synchronised

#Purposes of processing

  • Transcribing meeting audio and generating notes
  • Storing, searching, sharing and exporting notes
  • Referring to meeting content and generating responses through the chat feature
  • Administering workspaces and controlling permissions
  • Maintaining the availability of the service, responding to faults and detecting misuse
  • Responding to enquiries from the controller

#Duration of processing

From the day the controller begins using the service until the day this addendum ends and the return or deletion under Article 15 is complete. Where the controller sets a retention period using the service's features, however, processing of the data concerned ends when that retention period expires.

#Handling of sensitive personal information

Controller personal data is not, as a rule, to contain sensitive personal information (Article 2, item 3). What is said in a meeting may, however, include a medical history, health check results, a disability, a creed, a criminal record or other sensitive personal information; obtaining individuals' consent to acquiring that is the controller's responsibility under Article 3, paragraph 5.

A breach of personal data containing sensitive personal information is reportable to the Personal Information Protection Commission regardless of how many individuals are involved (Enforcement Rule 7, quoted under Article 12). For practice where what is said in a meeting may include sensitive personal information, see Use in healthcare, finance and the professions.

#Schedule 2 Security measures

In respect of controller personal data, the processor establishes a basic policy on the handling of personal data, puts in place handling rules covering each stage from acquisition to deletion, and takes the following measures. Detailed access control settings, how unauthorised access is detected and other matters whose disclosure would risk prejudicing security are not set out in this schedule, and are dealt with through the audit in Article 13 or in answer to individual enquiries. The explanation of each measure for controllers is published in Our security arrangements.

#Organisational security measures

Item What is done
Appointing a responsible person A person responsible for the handling of personal data is appointed, with their authority and responsibilities clearly defined
Limiting who handles data The staff who handle controller personal data, and the scope of what they handle, are defined and kept to the minimum necessary
Keeping track of processing Records of use, of the granting, changing and removal of permissions, and of data taken out are kept, with arrangements in place for reviewing them
Reporting lines Reporting lines are in place for where a breach of the handling rules, or a sign of one, is identified
Periodic review Processing is reviewed periodically and the results reported to the responsible person
Managing processors Criteria for selecting sub-processors are set, contracts are concluded, and how they process data is kept under periodic review
Responding to breaches The procedure for responding to a breach is documented, with deadlines for notification and reporting

#Personnel security measures

Item What is done
Confidentiality obligations Confidentiality agreements are concluded with all staff. The obligations survive the end of employment
Training Training on the handling of personal data is provided when staff start work and periodically thereafter
Reviewing permissions Permissions are granted only to the extent needed for the work, and reviewed promptly on a transfer or departure
Secrecy of communications Staff are made aware of how to handle information learnt in connection with features that carry exchanges between users

#Physical security measures

Item What is done
Data centres Servers are housed in facilities with entry control, monitoring and redundant power and cooling
Managing devices Disk encryption and screen locking are mandatory on work devices
Managing media Procedures are set for carrying equipment and electronic media containing personal data
Disposal Equipment and electronic media are disposed of by means that prevent recovery

#Technical security measures

Item What is done
Access control Access to controller personal data is limited to staff who need it for their work
Authentication Multi-factor authentication is applied to access to the processor's internal systems. Authentication of service users is delegated to the identity provider the controller uses
Encryption in transit Traffic between devices and servers, and between servers, is encrypted
Encryption at rest Stored controller personal data is encrypted
Separation Data is separated per workspace and not intermingled with other controllers' data
Logging Records of access and operations are collected and retained
Vulnerability management Procedures are in place for collecting vulnerability information and applying patches
Monitoring Mechanisms for detecting unauthorised access and anomalous behaviour are operated

#Understanding the external environment

Item What is done
Knowing the countries involved The countries in which controller personal data is processed, and in which the servers sit, are established
Knowing the regime The personal data protection regime of those countries (including any regime on government access to information) is established
Taking measures In light of that, encryption in transit and at rest, limits on retention, contractual restrictions on processing and other necessary measures are taken
Providing information to the controller On request, the name of the country, the name of the country the servers are in, and the measures taken are provided to the controller
Periodic review Whether the regime has changed is checked periodically, and the measures reviewed where necessary

補足 本覚書は契約書のひな形です。締結の前に、{{COMPANY}}の法務部門による内容の確認と、空欄になっている事項の確定が必要です。本文中の〔 〕は、締結時に具体的な内容を記入する欄で、委託元の商号（前文）、記録の保存期間（第8条）、再委託先の通知と異議申立ての日数（第9条）、開示等への協力期限（第11条）、漏えい等の通知期限（第12条）、監査の条件（第13条）、消去の期限（第15条）、損害賠償の上限（第16条）、再委託先の一覧（別紙3）が該当します。 本覚書は、 利用規約 の一部を構成します。個人データの取扱いに関する事項について本覚書と利用規約の定めが異なる場合は、本覚書が優先します。それ以外の事項については利用規約が適用されます。{{COMPANY}}自身が個人情報取扱事業者として取り扱う個人情報については、 プライバシーポリシー の定めによります。 セキュリティ体制 別紙2の前提となる安全管理措置の詳細 → セキュリティ・プライバシーに関するFAQ
